title: Choose the visual world for the rr web console
question: The roll assigned Carbon Copy Docket (grounded candidate 7 of 7). Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or steer.

options.label: Carbon Copy Docket
options.lineage: NCR triplicate carbon-copy business forms and dockets, 1950s–70s
options.thesis: Every write is a docketed triplicate: the send gate, the audit anchor and the encrypted backup are the three copies you can see. The console is one continuous form: docketed, stamped, tearable.
materials: NCR carbonless stock (bone / pale pink / pale green copies)
options.viewport: A perforated stub rail on the left carries docket numbers and revision pins; the working form fills the centre as ruled boxes (the review queue); every confirmed action stamps its three copies — GATE, AUDIT, BACKUP — so evidence is visible, not promised.
options.risk: Form density can tip into bureaucracy; the stamps must stay marks of control, never clutter.

raised.raise: Every confirmed send carries a human sign-off mark in the margin — the machine never signs for you.
The construction grid stays visible as hairline ruling in empty areas — the machine shows its work.

options.label: Par Avion Dispatch
options.lineage: registered airmail stationery: par-avion borders, franking marks, registration stubs
options.thesis: The console as a registered dispatch desk: every outbound reply is tracked mail with its stub, and the confirmed-send boundary is a postal one.
options.viewport: The outbox as registered mail slots; red/blue hairline stripes mark only the confirmed-send boundary; each sent reply tears its registration stub into the audit trail.
options.risk: Its decorative border is one hairline from costume; it must stay hairline weight and mark only the send boundary.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable as tinted glass slides on a lit goldenrod bed
options.thesis: One single type size for the whole console; rank is carried by weight, case, reversal and rules alone.
options.viewport: The review queue as a raked rack of slides; one opaque reversed plate marks the item in focus; a tick rail shows position and extent at every width.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the queue becomes a rack of slides and the one-size discipline is superb for density; holds product clarity, loses identification — timetables are not the job seeker's artifact.
options.risk: The 11-degree rake must never shear a text field or a form input.

options.label: J-Card Ledger
options.lineage: hand-ruled mixtape j-cards: side a / side b tracklists timed to fill exactly forty-five minutes
options.thesis: Send limits as timed sides: the day's budget fills exactly and physically cannot overflow.
options.viewport: Daily sending shown as a ruled side that fills to its minute cap; tentative drafts are penciled, confirmed sends are inked; the flip between automatic and manual mode is a physical side flip.
options.case: Holds product clarity through the capacity metaphor (send caps are literally fillable and non-overflowable); identification moderate — a personal artifact of careful planning.
options.risk: Hand-lettering drifts into whimsy in a tool that sends real mail to real recruiters.

options.label: Guide-Map Lobes
options.lineage: zoo and gardens guide maps: flat colour lobes whose coastline does all the dividing
options.thesis: One review item swells to dominate the workspace; its coastline, not a divider, separates work areas.
options.viewport: The active item is one lobe that swells until its coast leaves the frame on two sides; the queue shrinks to a coastline of pins; state is a capsule riding the coast's trailing edge.
options.case: Holds clarity: one-review-item-at-a-time is the product's true rhythm and the lobe makes it spatial; loses identification (park maps belong to a day out).
options.risk: A map is a picture before it is a tool; every control must stay a standard web control.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: a working spectrogram plate: one off-centre calibrated rail, colour as hairline emission lines only
options.thesis: State is line form, not hue: solid is live, dashed is pending, struck is disabled; colour does data only.
options.viewport: Every destination is a tick on one off-centre rail; the open view blooms into a bone-on-ash plate above it; queue state rides the rail as solid, dashed or struck hairlines.
options.case: Holds product clarity, and its state discipline is the accessibility requirement itself (colorblind-safe, form-first state); identification low — an instrument's world, not the seeker's.
options.risk: A one-rail topology can underuse the width of a review workspace.

options.label: Design Annual Plate Section
options.lineage: a design annual's plate section: registration crosshairs, hairline credits, one periwinkle sign-off stamp
options.case: Fuses poorly: a design annual is not the job seeker's world; loses both axes to the docket.
options.kept: Registration furniture and the human sign-off stamp: every confirmed send carries a margin mark proving a person approved it.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel gridded type specimens: letterforms built cell by cell on a visible construction grid
options.case: Fuses poorly: type-specimen culture is not the audience's; loses both axes to the docket.
options.kept: The construction grid stays visible as design — the machine shows its own working.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The three-pane mail client with a settings dashboard — sidebar, list, reading pane — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every mail-tool user expects, at full craft: navigation left, review queue centre, detail right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
